_comment: EXAMPLE · Db2 source / queries — what a SQL publisher runs. Unlike a file source, a SQL source is SINGLE mode: one frame per query slot, never a list, and query i feeds parameter i and lands in output_tables[i]. Five publishers over a db2 domain seeded with the world model: read_one_query, read_many_queries (three queries in ONE session, so the three tables cannot disagree — the reason to group related reads), read_without_transaction (transactional=False: a connection and an autocommit per query, no cross-query consistency), read_with_type_hints (schema_overrides: one {column: DataType} entry per query, None to leave one inferred), read_no_rows (the slot is None -> publish NO version, versus publishing an empty one). Also note table names are unique per COLLECTION, which is why read_one_query's output is `country_only`. One function per file under functions/db2_src_queries/. Run: `tdd xp one-shot --suite examples/db2_src_queries`.
